profile.name: Nashra Sundhu
profile.writeup:
Quietly determined, understated, and mathematically precise in her craft, Nashra Sandhu has long been the backbone of the Pakistan women spin attack. Born in Lahore, she does not rely on theatrics or aggressive send-offs, letting her subtle loop, drift, and pinpoint accuracy dismantle opposing batting lineups. Over almost a decade in top-flight international cricket, she has forged a reputation as one of the most economical and dependable slow left-arm orthodox bowlers in the world, capable of strangling run rates and forcing false strokes from the best batters across the globe.


Sandhu discovered her love for the game in Lahore, working her way up from school and club grounds into the city senior regional side around 2014. Her calm demeanor under pressure stood out early, earning her a spot in the Pakistan squad for the ICC Women World Cup Qualifiers in Colombo in February 2017. Making her ODI debut against South Africa on February 7, 2017, she instantly made her mark by picking up three wickets for 51 runs. A few months later at the 2017 Women Cricket World Cup in England, she authored an unforgettable performance against India, claiming four wickets for just 26 runs in a masterclass of left-arm orthodox bowling.


Following her World Cup exploits, Sandhu made her T20 debut against New Zealand in Sharjah in November 2017. She quickly adapted to the shortest format, proving that her trajectory and flight were just as effective in restricting boundaries as they were in long 50-over spells. She represented Pakistan at consecutive ICC Women T20 World Cups in the West Indies in 2018, Australia in 2020, and South Africa in 2023. In the 2023 T20 World Cup, her four wickets against Ireland were a testament to her unrelenting consistency, helping her climb into the top ten of
the official ICC bowling rankings.


Beyond her international exploits, Sandhu remained a stalwart in domestic cricket, representing Lahore, PCB Dynamites, and the Strikers with distinction. Her record in familiar subcontinent conditions made her a fearsome opponent, highlighted by her tally of over 20 ODI wickets at
the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore alone. During 2024, she continued to anchor the bowling attack during bilateral tours against the West Indies and England, and later starred at the ICC Women T20 World Cup held in the UAE, taking crucial top-order wickets against heavyweights like
Australia and Bangladesh with an economy rate that remained exceptionally low.


The year 2025 was another landmark year in Sandhu international journey. She was pivotal in Pakistan campaign at the ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier in April 2025, producing match-winning spells of two wickets in tight overs to seal Pakistan qualification. Later in October 2025
at the ICC Women Cricket World Cup, she consistently struck against elite batting orders, picking up crucial scalps against Australia and Bangladesh. Her mastery of line and length ensured that even on flat batting tracks, opposing batters were forced to take undue risks
against her frugal bowling.


In 2026, Sandhu continued her rich vein of form across both T20 and ODI formats during challenging tours of South Africa and Sri Lanka, followed by the Women Asia Cup T20 in Dubai in September 2026. Surpassing 100 international wickets across formats and remaining comfortably seated among the top-ranked bowlers globally, she has evolved from a quiet newcomer into a seasoned senior mentor. In a side experiencing generational transition, her ice-cool composure, tactical intelligence, and unwavering discipline ensure she remains an indispensable match-winner for Pakistan.
